_comment: The deploy contract (#32). Every path and basename the shipped stack agrees on,
stated ONCE. src/layout/gen.py turns this into gen/shim_paths.h and gen/shim_paths.sh;
no module under src/ may restate one of these literals — check.py fails the build if
one reappears. A GUI installer can read this file directly rather than the scripts.
atoms are literal; joins are composed from earlier names, so even a composite path
(C:\shim\steamclient64.dll) exists in exactly one place. sep is 'win' (backslash)
or 'posix' (slash). guard=true adds the value to check.py's drift guard: it may not
appear as a literal in any source under src/ outside this file.
switches are the runtime policy half (#33): one env var, one default, one predicate name.
gen.py emits the predicate into gen/shim_policy.h and gen/shim_policy.sh, and check.py
guards the env var name the same way it guards a path -- no site may re-derive the rule.
Relative names (*_REL, *_SUBDIR) are relative to a root the caller supplies -- $HOME
for the macOS ones, the bottle dir for the bottle ones. The manifest deliberately
holds no absolute unix path: $HOME belongs to whoever is running, not to the contract.

atoms.name: PE64
atoms.what: shim PE loaded by steam_api64.dll

atoms.name: PE32
atoms.what: shim PE loaded by steam_api.dll

atoms.name: UNIX64
atoms.what: unix half, under the 64-bit PE's basename

atoms.name: UNIX32
atoms.what: the same unix half under the 32-bit PE's basename

atoms.name: INJECT64
atoms.what: overlay injector for 64-bit titles

atoms.name: INJECT32
atoms.what: overlay injector for 32-bit titles

atoms.name: ENABLER
atoms.what: the m_bCompatEnabled injector

atoms.name: LAUNCH_SH
atoms.what: the compat-tool launch script

atoms.name: PATHS_SH
atoms.what: this manifest's sh fragment, deployed beside the launch script

atoms.name: POLICY_SH
atoms.what: this manifest's sh switch predicates, deployed beside the launch script

atoms.name: TOOL_VDF
atoms.what: Steam's compat-tool registration

atoms.name: TOOL_MANIFEST
atoms.what: Valve's compat-tool runtime manifest

atoms.name: TOOL_NAME
atoms.what: compat-tool dir name; must match the vdf's tool key

atoms.name: COMPAT_TOOLS
atoms.what: the dir STEAM_EXTRA_COMPAT_TOOLS_PATHS points at

atoms.name: DIST
atoms.what: built-artifact dir, in the repo and in the payload

atoms.name: VERSIONS
atoms.what: under the payload root: one dir per deployed version, so a rollback is a symlink swap

atoms.name: CURRENT
atoms.what: symlink beside them naming the live version; every consumer path goes through it

atoms.name: RECEIPT
atoms.what: what the last deploy laid down: version, files, hashes. Verify and uninstall read it

atoms.name: BOTTLE_DEFAULT
atoms.what: default CrossOver bottle name (SHIM_BOTTLE overrides)

atoms.name: SHIM_DIR_WIN
atoms.what: in-bottle payload dir, as the PE side sees it

atoms.name: SHIM_SUBDIR
atoms.what: the same dir relative to the bottle, unix side

atoms.name: PAYLOAD_REL
atoms.what: external payload root, relative to $HOME

atoms.name: LOG_DIR_REL
atoms.what: where all three logs land, relative to $HOME

atoms.name: STEAM_MACOS_REL
atoms.what: native Steam's MacOS dir, relative to $HOME

atoms.name: CX_BOTTLES_REL
atoms.what: CrossOver's bottle root, relative to $HOME

atoms.name: CX_APP_REL
atoms.what: CrossOver.app, relative to $HOME

atoms.name: STEAM_APP_REL
atoms.what: Valve's installer-placed bundle, relative to $HOME or to /. NOT where we exec Steam from — STEAM_MACOS_REL is. This one exists only to tell 'Steam is not installed' apart from 'Steam is installed and has never been run', which are one stat call and two entirely different remedies

atoms.name: LAUNCHER_REL
atoms.what: our launcher .app, relative to $HOME

atoms.name: LAUNCHER_BIN
atoms.what: the .app's CFBundleExecutable — the name deploy.sh writes and the bundle names back

atoms.name: SETTINGS_APP
atoms.what: nested helper app inside the launcher bundle: same binary, settings flag, so Spotlight finds the pane without the option-click trick

atoms.name: BUNDLE_ID
atoms.what: the launcher bundle's identifier

atoms.name: SETTINGS_ID
atoms.what: the nested settings helper's identifier — distinct, or LaunchServices sees two bundles claiming one id

atoms.name: PREFS_DOMAIN
atoms.what: UserDefaults suite both binaries read, named explicitly so the two bundle ids do not each get their own store. Deliberately NOT guarded: it is a prefix of both bundle ids, so guarding it would flag every legitimate use of those

atoms.name: PREF_OVERLAY
atoms.what: the launcher's stored overlay preference, in that suite. deploy.sh writes it when --overlay is passed and the launcher reads it at exec, so the two must agree on the key

atoms.name: SETTINGS_FLAG
atoms.what: the argument that turns the launcher into the settings pane; what the nested helper passes

atoms.name: DIAGNOSE_FLAG
atoms.what: print the diagnose report to stdout and exit — support surface, and what makes the pane's findings testable

atoms.name: PRINT_ENV_FLAG
atoms.what: print the environment the launcher WOULD exec Steam with, and exit; how check_launch_env.sh asks the merge question without launching Steam

atoms.name: STEAM_OSX
atoms.what: Valve's inner executable, the launcher's exec target

atoms.name: STEAM_DYLIB
atoms.what: the native client the unix half dlopens

atoms.name: OVERLAY_DYLIB
atoms.what: Valve's overlay renderer (ADR 0003)

atoms.name: LOG_LAUNCH
atoms.what: the launch script's log

atoms.name: LOG_UNIX
atoms.what: the unix half's log

atoms.name: LOG_ENABLER
atoms.what: the compat-gate injector's log

atoms.name: LSTEAM_PE64
atoms.what: the shim PE built under a SECOND name, for the DRM route (ADR 0014). Valve's signed steamclient64.dll keeps that basename, and two modules cannot share one in a process — so the shim is BUILT as this, never renamed: ntdll derives a builtin's unix half from the PE's internal name, not its filename

atoms.name: LSTEAM_UNIX64
atoms.what: its unix half, under the same basename

atoms.name: SHADOW_TIER0
atoms.what: our shadow of Valve's support lib: the only non-system import of steamclient64.dll we hook, and where the trampolines are installed (ADR 0014)

atoms.name: SHADOW_VSTDLIB
atoms.what: the other one, inert. Valve's real vstdlib initialises against tier0, so it cannot be left real while tier0 is shadowed

atoms.name: VALVE_PE64
atoms.what: Valve's OWN signed client DLL, under a name of ours. Deliberately not its own basename: Wine resolves a builtin by basename off the DLL path, and our shim sits on that path — same basename and OURS would load in its place, silently, and the wrapper would reject the unsigned file it found. Renaming costs nothing, because the wrapper reads whatever file provided CreateInterface and checks the BYTES

atoms.name: VSTEAM_DIR_WIN
atoms.what: in-bottle dir holding Valve's signed steamclient64.dll and our two shadows, as the PE side sees it. Separate from the shim dir so the DRM route cannot shadow the normal one

atoms.name: VSTEAM_SUBDIR
atoms.what: the same dir relative to the bottle, unix side

atoms.name: CLIENT_CACHE
atoms.what: payload subdir holding the Valve DLLs fetched from Valve's public client manifest. Beside the versions, not inside one: it outlives any single deploy and a re-download is expensive

atoms.name: CLIENT_MANIFEST_URL
atoms.what: Valve's own public, unauthenticated Windows client manifest — the same one steamcmd bootstraps from. Names the packages, their sizes and their SHA-256s

atoms.name: CLIENT_PKG
atoms.what: the package in that manifest carrying steamclient64.dll, tier0_s64.dll and vstdlib_s64.dll

atoms.name: FETCH_SH
atoms.what: the downloader that fills that cache, deployed beside the launch script. A contract name because the app runs it: the launcher, Diagnose and the pre-launch check all invoke this one file rather than each knowing how to talk to Valve's manifest (#105)

joins.name: PE64_WIN
joins.what: what SteamClientDll64 must point at

joins.name: PE32_WIN
joins.what: what SteamClientDll must point at

joins.name: INJECT64_WIN
joins.what: the injector the launch script execs

joins.name: VERSIONS_REL
joins.what: where a deploy unpacks a version, relative to $HOME

joins.name: LIVE_REL
joins.what: the live version through the symlink — what every consumer path below is built on, so an update never rewrites a consumer

joins.name: RECEIPT_REL
joins.what: the deploy receipt, beside the versions rather than inside one: it outlives any single version

joins.name: COMPAT_TOOLS_REL
joins.what: STEAM_EXTRA_COMPAT_TOOLS_PATHS, relative to $HOME

joins.name: TOOL_DIR_REL
joins.what: the deployed compat tool, relative to $HOME

joins.name: ENABLER_REL
joins.what: DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES target, relative to $HOME

joins.name: STEAM_OSX_REL
joins.what: the launcher's exec target, relative to $HOME

joins.name: STEAM_DYLIB_REL
joins.what: dlopen target, relative to $HOME

joins.name: OVERLAY_DYLIB_REL
joins.what: renderer dlopen target, relative to $HOME

joins.name: LOG_LAUNCH_REL
joins.what: relative to $HOME

joins.name: LOG_UNIX_REL
joins.what: relative to $HOME

joins.name: LOG_ENABLER_REL
joins.what: relative to $HOME

joins.name: VALVE_PE64_WIN
joins.what: what SteamClientDll64 points at on the DRM route: VALVE'S signed DLL, not ours

joins.name: LSTEAM_PE64_WIN
joins.what: the shim under its second name, which the trampolines load

joins.name: CLIENT_CACHE_REL
joins.what: the fetched Valve DLLs, relative to $HOME

joins.name: CLIENT_DLL_REL
joins.what: Valve's signed client DLL in that cache, relative to $HOME. The one file of the DRM route that we do not ship and cannot: 'has the fetch run on this machine' is a stat of exactly this path, and it is asked from the launch script, the preflight list and Diagnose

joins.name: FETCH_SH_REL
joins.what: the deployed downloader, relative to $HOME — what the launcher app execs when the cache is empty

switches.name: OVERLAY

veto.what: Steam's OWN answer for this launch, set by the client when 'Enable the Steam Overlay while in-game' is off -- globally (Settings -> In Game) or for this title (Properties -> General). Measured, not assumed: absent for a default-on title, '1' the very next launch after the per-game box is unticked, with no Steam restart, so it reports live state rather than the last flush (#92). NOT SteamNoOverlayUIDrawing, which is the renderer's own flag and a different question

switches.what: whether the Steam overlay is delivered: the unixlib dlopens Valve's renderer, the PE half binds the seam in DllMain and hooks CreateProcess, and the launch script routes through the injector (ADR 0003, ADR 0006). Steam's per-title setting vetoes it (ADR 0012)

switches.name: DRM
switches.what: whether a DRM-wrapped title is launched through Valve's own signed steamclient64.dll with its exports trampolined into our shim (ADR 0014). ON by default, but conditional on delivery the way the overlay is: no fetched Valve DLL means the route is unavailable and the launch falls back to the normal one. Only titles whose EXE carries a .bind section take it at all, so a non-DRM title's path is byte-identical to what it was before this existed
